prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company for all customers — the right contractor depends on your budget, timeline, the scope of work, and how well they communicate and meet your needs. I can, however, help you find the best option in St. Louis by pointing you to highly reliable ways to choose and what to look for.

How to find top interior painters in St. Louis
- Check review sites and ratings: Google, Yelp, Angi (formerly Angie’s List), Houzz, and the BBB. Read multiple recent reviews (last 12–24 months).
- Ask neighbors or local Facebook groups/Nextdoor for personal referrals.
- Look for portfolios/photos of completed projects to match the style and quality you want.
- Verify insurance and (if applicable) licensing and local business registration.
- Confirm they provide written estimates, a clear scope of work, and a warranty/guarantee.

What to ask when getting quotes
- Do you carry liability insurance and worker’s comp? Can you provide certificates?
- Can you provide local references or recent project photos?
- What brands and sheens of paint do you use? Do you offer color consultation?
- What surface prep is included (repairs, sanding, priming, drywall/caulk repair)?
- How many coats and what coverage are included? Are caulking and trim included in the price?
- What is the timeline and project start date? Who will supervise the work?
- What is your payment schedule? Do you require a deposit?
- Do you provide a written contract and a satisfaction/warranty policy?

Typical price expectations (ballpark)
- Single room (walls only): roughly $300–$800 depending on size and prep.
- Whole-house interior: commonly $2,000–$7,000+, depending on number of rooms, ceilings, trim work, and prep.
(Prices vary by company, paint quality, and amount of prep/repairs.)

Red flags
- No written estimate or contract
- No insurance or unwillingness to provide proof
- Extremely low bids far below others (often leads to shortcuts)
- No local references or portfolio
- Pushy sales tactics or pressure to sign immediately

If you want, I can:
- Pull together a short list of top-rated interior painters in St. Louis if you give a ZIP code or neighborhood (I can’t browse the web directly in this chat, but I can tell you how to search or craft messages to send to contractors).
- Help you compare 3 quotes if you paste them here.
- Draft an email or checklist you can send to painters to get comparable estimates.

Tell me your ZIP code, your project details (rooms, walls vs. trim/ceilings, any repairs), and any preferences (paint brand, color help, budget) and I’ll help you narrow the best options.
